product: Cratebeam, a morning exception digest for fulfillment depots

flaws.cause: Cratebeam would charge for the same digest, assignments and weekly report that all launch depots already receive in LaneSkein. The current option is available, suitable and demonstrably reduces review time to the target range. Research identifies no improvement in coverage, control or results to justify another product.

evidence.what: Morning List is included and enabled for all twenty depots, covers the proposed functions, and meets the review-time goal in observed use.
These categories and owner assignments constitute the cohort's complete morning-review need.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Do not fund a separate equivalent subscription; use the existing option or identify a supported unmet benefit before choosing a new offer.
flaws.fix: Confirm an incremental customer benefit before funding a new product. If the stated goal remains morning review time, help customers use Morning List instead.

flaws.cause: The plan permanently sells the training catalog and accepts a five-year noncompete for $40,000. The existing line generates $90,000 quarterly contribution, has signed renewals and can coexist with software; the software budget is already funded. No cost of keeping the line or route back is provided for this irreversible business decision.

evidence.what: The profitable, lightly maintained line has signed renewals, no forced-sale condition and no repurchase or license-back right.
The software cohort fits existing available staffing.

flaws.changes_what_gets_built: Keep the training business or choose a reversible staffing arrangement instead of transferring permanent rights as a launch condition.
flaws.fix: Separate the product test from disposal of the training asset. Retain the catalog unless an explicit economic case and acceptable exit terms support a sale.

notes: The permanent catalog transfer is a business commitment, not a data-deletion or implementation issue.
